name: Anna Neumann
headline: Researcher @Max-Planck | Env. Engineering x Entrepreneurship | TUM, CDTM, MIT, Berkeley 🌏🌱✨
summary:
🌱I am an Environmental Engineering x Management student, passionate about driving sustainable change for a green and equitable future.

🌏 As I have learned to view today’s global crises as challenges and our economic system as an enabler to solve them, I want to leverage my education and career to build an economy serving people, planet, and prosperity.

✨Currently looking for opportunities in climate (and policy) research, operational positions in global organizations driving sustainable development, or just connecting about the topic. Hit me up!

-----------

To give you a debrief of my academic, professional, and extracurricular journey to date:

🧑🏼‍🎓 During my interdisciplinary bachelor’s degree in Management and Technology, I have built knowledge in business, economics, and computer engineering. Further, I worked on sustainability-related projects, s.a., conceptualizing a solar investment product for carbon offsetting and prototyping a gamified carbon footprint application.

👩🏽‍💻 Professionally, I bring industry experience in Circular Economy, Carbon Accounting & Management, Energy and Metals. I gained valuable skills interning at impact-oriented tech startups and top-tier strategy consulting firms with the overarching goal of decarbonizing industries: I co-developed carbon accounting software, strategized on green metal commercialization, and assessed energy management systems (among other things).

👷🏻‍♀️ I strive the most when working on impactful real-world projects around the globe. In the past, I led Team glassic in setting up a circular beverage startup in Thailand to tackle plastic pollution. Moreover, I have volunteered for GainForest in Colombia, a decentralized fund utilizing AI and ML to advance measurement, verification, and reporting (MRV) processes for forest conservation and climate finance.

🏔 In my free time, I love hiking & traveling, building new movement skills in the gym, or going ice bathing.

positions.title: Researcher
positions.company: Max Planck Institute for Innovation and Competition
positions.description: At the Net Zero Lab, I am conducting research around the Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) with a focus on Avoided Deforestation projects. My research aims to better understand the success factors of Avoided Deforestation projects in offsetting the amount of carbon claimed by project developers.

positions.title: Research Scholar & Project Manager
positions.description:
As part of the Harvard–MIT Global Climate Policy Project (GCPP), our team–together with an expert working group–developed a flagship proposal for a climate coalition to align carbon pricing and border carbon adjustments. The proposal was highlighted as one of Brazil's priority topics for COP30, and informs the Presidency’s Council of Economists.

- I managed the internal research team of 7, coordinating writing, editing, and publication of a 100+ page flagship report launched at Harvard Climate Action Week and New York Climate Week
- I led research on (i) coalition principles and (ii) technology transfer policies to enable industry decarbonization in low- and middle-income countries.

company.name: Max Planck Institute for Innovation and Competition
company.tagline: We are committed to legal and economic research on processes of innovation and competition and their regulation.
company.description:
We are committed to fundamental legal and economic research on processes of innovation and competition and their regulation. Our research focuses on the incentives, determinants and implications of innovation. With an outstanding international team of scholars and excellent scientific and administrative infrastructure including our renowned library, we host academics from all over the world and actively promote young researchers. Through dedicated educational efforts, we engage in the training and mentoring of early-career researchers and foster knowledge exchange with national and international institutions. We inform and guide legal and economic discourse on an impartial basis. As an independent research institution, we provide evidence-based research results to academia, policymakers, the private sector as well as the general public.
